3: '''
4: Overview:
5: 
6:     Build script for PyMuPDF, supporting PEP-517 and simple command-line usage.
7: 
8:     We hard-code the URL of the MuPDF .tar.gz file that we require. This
9:     generally points to a particular source release on mupdf.com.
10: 
11:     Default behaviour:
12: 
13:         Building an sdist:
14:             As of 2024-002-28 we no longer download the MuPDF .tar.gz file and
15:             embed it within the sdist. Instead it will be downloaded at build
16:             time.
17: 
18:         Building PyMuPDF:
19:             We first download the hard-coded mupdf .tar.gz file.
20: 
21:             Then we extract and build MuPDF locally, before building PyMuPDF
22:             itself. So PyMuPDF will always be built with the exact MuPDF
23:             release that we require.
24: 
25: 
26: Environmental variables:
27: 
28:     If building with system MuPDF (PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD is empty string):
29:     
30:         CFLAGS
31:         CXXFLAGS
32:         LDFLAGS
33:             Added to c, c++, and link commands.
34:         
35:         PYMUPDF_INCLUDES
36:             Colon-separated extra include paths.
37:         
38:         PYMUPDF_MUPDF_LIB
39:             Directory containing MuPDF libraries, (libmupdf.so,
40:             libmupdfcpp.so).
41:     
42:     PIPCL_SHOW_ENV
43:         If '0', we do not show environment variables on startup.
44:     
45:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_DEVENV
46:         Location of devenv.com on Windows. If unset we search for it - see
47:         wdev.py. if that fails we use just 'devenv.com'.
48: 
49:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_DUMMY
50:         If 1, we build dummy sdist and wheel with no files.
51:     
52:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR
53:         Control building of separate wheels for PyMuPDF.
54:         
55:         Must be unset or a combination of 'p', 'b' and 'd'.
56:         
57:         Default is 'pbd'.
58:         
59:         'p':
60:             Generated wheel contains PyMuPDF code.
61:         'b':
62:             Generated wheel contains MuPDF libraries; these are independent of
63:             the Python version.
64:         'd':
65:             Generated wheel contains includes and libraries for MuPDF.
66:         
67:         If 'p' is included, the generated wheel is called PyMuPDF.
68:         Otherwise if 'b' is included the generated wheel is called PyMuPDFb.
69:         Otherwise if 'd' is included the generated wheel is called PyMuPDFd.
70:         
71:         For example:
72:         
73:             'pb': a `PyMuPDF` wheel with PyMuPDF runtime files and MuPDF
74:             runtime shared libraries.
75:             
76:             'b': a `PyMuPDFb` wheel containing MuPDF runtime shared libraries.
77:             
78:             'pbd' a `PyMuPDF` wheel with PyMuPDF runtime files and MuPDF
79:             runtime shared libraries, plus MuPDF build-time files (includes,
80:             *.lib files on Windows).
81:             
82:             'd': a `PyMuPDFd` wheel containing MuPDF build-time files
83:             (includes, *.lib files on Windows).
84:     
85:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_LIBCLANG
86:         For internal testing.
87:         
88:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD
89:         If unset or '-', use internal hard-coded default MuPDF location.
90:         Otherwise overrides location of MuPDF when building PyMuPDF:
91:             Empty string:
92:                 Build PyMuPDF with the system MuPDF.
93:             A string starting with 'git:':
94:                 We use `git` commands to clone/update a local MuPDF checkout.
95:                 Should match `git:[--branch <branch>][--tag <tag>][<remote>]`.
96:                 If <remote> is omitted we use a default.
97:                 For example:
98:                     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD="git:--branch master"
99:                 Passed as <text> arg to pipcl.git_get().
100:             Otherwise:
101:                 Location of mupdf directory.
102:     
103:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BSYMBOLIC
104:         If '0' we do not link libmupdf.so with -Bsymbolic.
105:     
106:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TESSERACT
107:         If '0' we build MuPDF without Tesseract.
108:     
109:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD_TYPE
110:         Unix only. Controls build type of MuPDF. Supported values are:
111:             debug
112:             memento
113:             release (default)
114:     
115:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL
116:         If '1' we (incorrectly) claim we are thread-safe.
117: 
118:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_CLEAN
119:         Unix only. If '1', we do a clean MuPDF build.
120: 
121:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF
122:         Should be preprocessor statement to enable MuPDF reference count
123:         checking.
124:         
125:         As of 2024-09-27, MuPDF default is `#ifndef NDEBUG`.
126: 
127:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF
128:         Should be preprocessor statement to enable MuPDF runtime diagnostics in
129:         response to environment variables such as MUPDF_trace.
130:         
131:         As of 2024-09-27, MuPDF default is `#ifndef NDEBUG`.
132: 
133:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_THIRD
134:         If '0' and we are building on Linux with the system MuPDF
135:         (i.e. PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD=''), then don't link with
136:         `-lmupdf-third`.
137:     
138:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_VS_UPGRADE
139:         If '1' we run mupdf `scripts/mupdfwrap.py` with `--vs-upgrade 1` to
140:         help Windows builds work with Visual Studio versions newer than 2019.
141: 
142:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TGZ
143:         If set, overrides location of MuPDF .tar.gz file:
144:             Empty string:
145:                 Do not download MuPDF .tar.gz file. Sdist's will not contain
146:                 MuPDF.
147: 
148:             A string containing '://':
149:                 The URL from which to download the MuPDF .tar.gz file. Leaf
150:                 must match mupdf-*.tar.gz.
151: 
152:             Otherwise:
153:                 The path of local mupdf git checkout. We put all files in this
154:                 checkout known to git into a local tar archive.
155: 
156:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_OVERWRITE_CONFIG
157:         If '0' we do not overwrite MuPDF's include/mupdf/fitz/config.h with
158:         PyMuPDF's own configuration file, before building MuPDF.
159:     
160:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REBUILD
161:         If 0 we do not (re)build mupdf.
162:     
163:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_PY_LIMITED_API
164:         If not '0', we build for current Python's stable ABI.
165:     
166:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_URL_WHEEL
167:         If set, we use an existing wheel instead of building a new wheel.
168:         
169:         If starts with `http://` or `https://`:
170:             If ends with '/', we append our wheel name and download. Otherwise
171:             we download directly.
172:         
173:         If starts with `file://`:
174:             If ends with '/' we look for a matching wheel name, `using
175:             pipcl.wheel_name_match()` to cope with differing platform tags,
176:             for example our `manylinux2014_x86_64` will match with an existing
177:             wheel with `manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64`.
178:         
179:         Any other prefix is an error.
180: 
181:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_SWIG
182:         If set, we use this instead of `swig`.
183:     
184:     WDEV_VS_YEAR
185:         If set, we use as Visual Studio year, for example '2019' or '2022'.
186: 
187:     WDEV_VS_GRADE
188:         If set, we use as Visual Studio grade, for example 'Community' or
189:         'Professional' or 'Enterprise'.

249: def _fs_remove(path):
250:     '''
251:     Removes file or directory, without raising exception if it doesn't exist.
252: 
253:     We assert-fail if the path still exists when we return, in case of
254:     permission problems etc.
255:     '''
256:     # First try deleting `path` as a file.
257:     try:
258:         os.remove( path)
259:     except Exception as e:
260:         pass
261:     
262:     if os.path.exists(path):
263:         # Try deleting `path` as a directory. Need to use
264:         # shutil.rmtree() callback to handle permission problems; see:
265:         # https://docs.python.org/3/library/shutil.html#rmtree-example
266:         #
267:         def error_fn(fn, path, excinfo):
268:             # Clear the readonly bit and reattempt the removal.
269:             os.chmod(path, stat.S_IWRITE)
270:             fn(path)
271:         shutil.rmtree( path, onerror=error_fn)
272:     
273:     assert not os.path.exists( path)

293: def tar_check(path, mode='r:gz', prefix=None, remove=False):
294:     '''
295:     Checks items in tar file have same <top-directory>, or <prefix> if not None.
296: 
297:     We fail if items in tar file have different top-level directory names.
298: 
299:     path:
300:         The tar file.
301:     mode:
302:         As tarfile.open().
303:     prefix:
304:         If not None, we fail if tar file's <top-directory> is not <prefix>.
305:     
306:     Returns the directory name (which will be <prefix> if not None).
307:     '''
308:     with tarfile.open( path, mode) as t:
309:         items = t.getnames()
310:         assert items
311:         item = items[0]
312:         assert not item.startswith('./') and not item.startswith('../')
313:         s = item.find('/')
314:         if s == -1:
315:             prefix_actual = item + '/'
316:         else:
317:             prefix_actual = item[:s+1]
318:         if prefix:
319:             assert prefix == prefix_actual, f'{path=} {prefix=} {prefix_actual=}'
320:         for item in items[1:]:
321:             assert item.startswith( prefix_actual), f'prefix_actual={prefix_actual!r} != item={item!r}'
322:     return prefix_actual

325: def tar_extract(path, mode='r:gz', prefix=None, exists='raise'):
326:     '''
327:     Extracts tar file into single local directory.
328:     
329:     We fail if items in tar file have different <top-directory>.
330: 
331:     path:
332:         The tar file.
333:     mode:
334:         As tarfile.open().
335:     prefix:
336:         If not None, we fail if tar file's <top-directory> is not <prefix>.
337:     exists:
338:         What to do if <top-directory> already exists:
339:             'raise': raise exception.
340:             'remove': remove existing file/directory before extracting.
341:             'return': return without extracting.
342:     
343:     Returns the directory name (which will be <prefix> if not None, with '/'
344:     appended if not already present).
345:     '''
346:     prefix_actual = tar_check( path, mode, prefix)
347:     if os.path.exists( prefix_actual):
348:         if exists == 'raise':
349:             raise Exception( f'Path already exists: {prefix_actual!r}')
350:         elif exists == 'remove':
351:             remove( prefix_actual)
352:         elif exists == 'return':
353:             log( f'Not extracting {path} because already exists: {prefix_actual}')
354:             return prefix_actual
355:         else:
356:             assert 0, f'Unrecognised exists={exists!r}'
357:     assert not os.path.exists( prefix_actual), f'Path already exists: {prefix_actual}'
358:     log( f'Extracting {path}')
359:     with tarfile.open( path, mode) as t:
360:         t.extractall()
361:     return prefix_actual

394: def git_patch(directory, patch, hard=False):
395:     '''
396:     Applies string <patch> with `git patch` in <directory>.
397:     
398:     If <hard> is true we clean the tree with `git checkout .` and then apply
399:     the patch.
400: 
401:     Otherwise we apply patch only if it is not already applied; this might fail
402:     if there are conflicting changes in the tree.
403:     '''
404:     log(f'Applying patch in {directory}:\n{textwrap.indent(patch, "    ")}')
405:     if not patch:
406:         return
407:     # Carriage returns break `git apply` so we use `newline='\n'` in open().
408:     path = os.path.abspath(f'{directory}/pymupdf_patch.txt')
409:     with open(path, 'w', newline='\n') as f:
410:         f.write(patch)
411:     log(f'Using patch file: {path}')
412:     if hard:
413:         run(f'cd {directory} && git checkout .')
414:         run(f'cd {directory} && git apply {path}')
415:         log(f'Have applied patch in {directory}.')
416:     else:
417:         e = run( f'cd {directory} && git apply --check --reverse {path}', check=0)
418:         if e == 0:
419:             log(f'Not patching {directory} because already patched.')
420:         else:
421:             run(f'cd {directory} && git apply {path}')
422:             log(f'Have applied patch in {directory}.')
423:     run(f'cd {directory} && git diff')

428: def get_mupdf_internal(out, location=None, local_tgz=None):
429:     '''
430:     Gets MuPDF as either a .tgz or a local directory.
431:     
432:     Args:
433:         out:
434:             Either 'dir' (we return name of local directory containing mupdf) or 'tgz' (we return
435:             name of local .tgz file containing mupdf).
436:         location:
437:             First, if None we set to hard-coded default URL or git location.
438:             If starts with 'git:', should be remote git location.
439:             Otherwise if containing '://' should be URL for .tgz.
440:             Otherwise should path of local mupdf checkout.
441:         local_tgz:
442:             If not None, must be local .tgz file.
443:     Returns:
444:         (path, location):
445:             `path` is absolute path of local directory or .tgz containing
446:             MuPDF, or None if we are to use system MuPDF.
447: 
448:             `location_out` is `location` if not None, else the hard-coded
449:             default location.
450:                 
451:     '''
452:     log(f'get_mupdf_internal(): {out=} {location=}')
453:     assert out in ('dir', 'tgz')
454:     if location is None:
455:         location = f'https://mupdf.com/downloads/archive/mupdf-{version_mupdf}-source.tar.gz'
456:         #location = 'git:--branch master https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf.git'
457:     
458:     if location == '':
459:         # Use system mupdf.
460:         return None, location
461:     
462:     local_dir = None
463:     if local_tgz:
464:         assert os.path.isfile(local_tgz)
465:     elif location.startswith( 'git:'):
466:         local_dir = 'mupdf-git'
467:         pipcl.git_get(local_dir, text=location, remote='https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf.git')
468:         
469:         # Show sha of checkout.
470:         run(
471:                 f'cd {local_dir} && git show --pretty=oneline|head -n 1',
472:                 check = False,
473:                 prefix = 'mupdf git id: ',
474:                 )
475:     elif '://' in location:
476:         # Download .tgz.
477:         local_tgz = os.path.basename( location)
478:         suffix = '.tar.gz'
479:         assert location.endswith(suffix), f'Unrecognised suffix in remote URL {location=}.'
480:         name = local_tgz[:-len(suffix)]
481:         log( f'Download {location=} {local_tgz=} {name=}')
482:         if os.path.exists(local_tgz):
483:             try:
484:                 tar_check(local_tgz, 'r:gz', prefix=f'{name}/')
485:             except Exception as e:
486:                 log(f'Not using existing file {local_tgz} because invalid tar data: {e}')
487:                 _fs_remove( local_tgz)
488:         if os.path.exists(local_tgz):
489:             log(f'Not downloading from {location} because already present: {local_tgz!r}')
490:         else:
491:             log(f'Downloading from {location=} to {local_tgz=}.')
492:             urllib.request.urlretrieve( location, local_tgz + '-')
493:             os.rename(local_tgz + '-', local_tgz)
494:             assert os.path.exists( local_tgz)
495:             tar_check( local_tgz, 'r:gz', prefix=f'{name}/')
496:     else:
497:         assert os.path.isdir(location), f'Local MuPDF does not exist: {location=}'
498:         local_dir = location
499:     
500:     assert bool(local_dir) != bool(local_tgz)
501:     if out == 'dir':
502:         if not local_dir:
503:             assert local_tgz
504:             local_dir = tar_extract( local_tgz, exists='return')
505:         return os.path.abspath( local_dir), location
506:     elif out == 'tgz':
507:         if not local_tgz:
508:             # Create .tgz containing git files in `local_dir`.
509:             assert local_dir
510:             if local_dir.endswith( '/'):
511:                 local_dir = local_dir[:-1]
512:             top = os.path.basename(local_dir)
513:             local_tgz = f'{local_dir}.tgz'
514:             log( f'Creating .tgz from git files. {top=} {local_dir=} {local_tgz=}')
515:             _fs_remove( local_tgz)
516:             with tarfile.open( local_tgz, 'w:gz') as f:
517:                 for name in pipcl.git_items( local_dir, submodules=True):
518:                     path = os.path.join( local_dir, name)
519:                     if os.path.isfile( path):
520:                         path2 = f'{top}/{name}'
521:                         log(f'Adding {path=} {path2=}.')
522:                         f.add( path, path2, recursive=False)
523:         return os.path.abspath( local_tgz), location
524:     else:
525:         assert 0, f'Unrecognised {out=}'
526:

576: def build():
577:     '''
578:     pipcl.py `build_fn()` callback.
579:     '''
580:     #pipcl.show_sysconfig()
581:     
582:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_DUMMY == '1':
583:         log(f'{PYMUPDF_SETUP_DUMMY=} Building dummy wheel with no files.')
584:         return list()
585:     
586:     # Download MuPDF.
587:     #
588:     mupdf_local, mupdf_location = get_mupdf()
589:     if mupdf_local:
590:         mupdf_version_tuple = get_mupdf_version(mupdf_local)
591:     # else we cannot determine version this way and do not use it
592: 
593:     build_type = os.environ.get( 'PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BUILD_TYPE', 'release')
594:     assert build_type in ('debug', 'memento', 'release'), \
595:             f'Unrecognised build_type={build_type!r}'
596:     
597:     overwrite_config = os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_OVERWRITE_CONFIG', '1') == '1'
598:     
599:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF = os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF')
600:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF = os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF')
601:     
602:     # Build MuPDF shared libraries.
603:     #
604:     if windows:
605:         mupdf_build_dir = build_mupdf_windows(
606:                 mupdf_local,
607:                 build_type,
608:                 overwrite_config,
609:                 g_py_limited_api,
610:                 PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF,
611:                 PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF,
612:                 PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL,
613:                 )
614:     else:
615:         if 'p' not in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR and 'b' not in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
616:             # We only need MuPDF headers, so no point building MuPDF.
617:             log(f'Not building MuPDF because not Windows and {PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR=}.')
618:             mupdf_build_dir = None
619:         else:
620:             mupdf_build_dir = build_mupdf_unix(
621:                     mupdf_local,
622:                     build_type,
623:                     overwrite_config,
624:                     g_py_limited_api,
625:                     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF,
626:                     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF,
627:                     PYMUPDF_SETUP_SWIG,
628:                     PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL,
629:                     )
630:     log( f'build(): mupdf_build_dir={mupdf_build_dir!r}')
631:     
632:     # Build `extra` module.
633:     #
634:     if 'p' in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
635:         path_so_leaf = _build_extension(
636:                 mupdf_local,
637:                 mupdf_build_dir,
638:                 build_type,
639:                 g_py_limited_api,
640:                 )
641:     else:
642:         log(f'Not building extension.')
643:         path_so_leaf = None
644:     
645:     # Generate list of (from, to) items to return to pipcl. What we add depends
646:     # on PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR.
647:     #
648:     ret = list()    
649:     def add(flavour, from_, to_):
650:         assert flavour in 'pbd'
651:         if flavour in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
652:             ret.append((from_, to_))
653:     
654:     to_dir = 'pymupdf/'
655:     to_dir_d = f'{to_dir}/mupdf-devel'
656:     
657:     # Add implementation files.
658:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/__init__.py', to_dir)
659:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/__main__.py', to_dir)
660:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/pymupdf.py', to_dir)
661:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/table.py', to_dir)
662:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/utils.py', to_dir)
663:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/_wxcolors.py', to_dir)
664:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/_apply_pages.py', to_dir)
665:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/build/extra.py', to_dir)
666:     add('p', b'', f'{to_dir}/py.typed')
667:     if path_so_leaf:
668:         add('p', f'{g_root}/src/build/{path_so_leaf}', to_dir)
669: 
670:     # Add support for `fitz` backwards compatibility.
671:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/fitz___init__.py', 'fitz/__init__.py')
672:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/fitz_table.py', 'fitz/table.py')
673:     add('p', f'{g_root}/src/fitz_utils.py', 'fitz/utils.py')
674: 
675:     if mupdf_local:
676:         # Add MuPDF Python API.
677:         add('p', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/mupdf.py', to_dir)
678: 
679:         # Add MuPDF shared libraries.
680:         if windows:
681:             wp = pipcl.wdev.WindowsPython()
682:             add('p', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/_mupdf.pyd', to_dir)
683:             add('b', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/mupdfcpp{wp.cpu.windows_suffix}.dll', to_dir)
684: 
685:             # Add Windows .lib files.
686:             mupdf_build_dir2 = _windows_lib_directory(mupdf_local, build_type)
687:             add('d', f'{mupdf_build_dir2}/mupdfcpp{wp.cpu.windows_suffix}.lib', f'{to_dir_d}/lib/')
688:             # MuPDF-1.25+ language bindings build also builds libmuthreads.
689:             add('d', f'{mupdf_build_dir2}/libmuthreads.lib', f'{to_dir_d}/lib/')
690:         elif darwin:
691:             add('p', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/_mupdf.so', to_dir)
692:             add('b', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdfcpp.so', to_dir)
693:             add('b', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdf.dylib', to_dir)
694:             add('d', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdf-threads.a', f'{to_dir_d}/lib/')
695:         elif pyodide:
696:             add('p', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/_mupdf.so', to_dir)
697:             add('b', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdfcpp.so', to_dir)
698:             add('b', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdf.so', to_dir)
699:         else:
700:             add('p', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/_mupdf.so', to_dir)
701:             add('b', pipcl.get_soname(f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdfcpp.so'), to_dir)
702:             add('b', pipcl.get_soname(f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdf.so'), to_dir)
703:             add('d', f'{mupdf_build_dir}/libmupdf-threads.a', f'{to_dir_d}/lib/')
704: 
705:         if 'd' in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
706:             # Add MuPDF C and C++ headers to `ret_d`. Would prefer to use
707:             # pipcl.git_items() but hard-coded mupdf tree is not a git
708:             # checkout.
709:             #
710:             for root in (
711:                     f'{mupdf_local}/include',
712:                     f'{mupdf_local}/platform/c++/include',
713:                     ):
714:                 for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
715:                     for filename in filenames:
716:                         if not filename.endswith('.h'):
717:                             continue
718:                         header_abs = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
719:                         assert header_abs.startswith(root)
720:                         header_rel = header_abs[len(root)+1:]
721:                         add('d', f'{header_abs}', f'{to_dir_d}/include/{header_rel}')
722:     
723:     # Add a .py file containing build-time information - location of MuPDF,
724:     # pymupdf git info, swig version etc.
725:     #
726:     swig = PYMUPDF_SETUP_SWIG or 'swig'
727:     swig_version_text = run(f'{swig} -version', capture=1)
728:     m = re.search('\nSWIG Version ([^\n]+)', swig_version_text)
729:     log(f'{swig_version_text=}')
730:     assert m, f'Unrecognised {swig_version_text=}'
731:     swig_version = m.group(1)
732:     def int_or_0(text):
733:         try:
734:             return int(text)
735:         except Exception:
736:             return 0
737:     swig_version_tuple = tuple(int_or_0(i) for i in swig_version.split('.'))
738:     version_p_tuple = tuple(int_or_0(i) for i in version_p.split('.'))
739:     log(f'{swig_version=}')
740:     text = ''
741:     text += pipcl.git_info_py(g_root, check=0, prefix = 'pymupdf_git_')
742:     text += f'mupdf_location = {mupdf_location!r}\n'
743:     text += f'pymupdf_version = {version_p!r}\n'
744:     text += f'pymupdf_version_tuple = {version_p_tuple!r}\n'
745:     text += f'swig_version = {swig_version!r}\n'
746:     text += f'swig_version_tuple = {swig_version_tuple!r}\n'
747:     text += f'fake_no_gil = {PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL=="1"!r}\n'
748:     log(f'_build.py is:\n{textwrap.indent(text, "    ")}')
749:     add('p', text.encode(), f'{to_dir}/_build.py')
750:     
751:     # Add single README file.
752:     if 'p' in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
753:         add('p', f'{g_root}/README.md', '$dist-info/README.md')
754:     elif 'b' in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
755:         add('b', f'{g_root}/READMEb.md', '$dist-info/README.md')
756:     elif 'd' in PYMUPDF_SETUP_FLAVOUR:
757:         add('d', f'{g_root}/READMEd.md', '$dist-info/README.md')
758:     
759:     return ret

762: def env_add(env, name, value, sep=' ', prepend=False, verbose=False):
763:     '''
764:     Appends/prepends `<value>` to `env[name]`.
765:     
766:     If `name` is not in `env`, we use os.environ[name] if it exists.
767:     '''
768:     v = env.get(name)
769:     if verbose:
770:         log(f'Initally: {name}={v!r}')
771:     if v is None:
772:         v = os.environ.get(name)
773:     if v is None:
774:         env[ name] = value
775:     else:
776:         if prepend:
777:             env[ name] =  f'{value}{sep}{v}'
778:         else:
779:             env[ name] =  f'{v}{sep}{value}'
780:     if verbose:
781:         log(f'Returning with {name}={env[name]!r}')

784: def build_mupdf_windows(
785:         mupdf_local,
786:         build_type,
787:         overwrite_config,
788:         g_py_limited_api,
789:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF,
790:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF,
791:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL,
792:         ):
793:     
794:     assert mupdf_local
795:     mupdf_version_tuple = get_mupdf_version(mupdf_local)
796:     log(f'{overwrite_config=}')
797:     log(f'{mupdf_version_tuple=}')
798:     wp = pipcl.wdev.WindowsPython()
799:     tesseract = '' if os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TESSERACT') == '0' else 'tesseract-'
800:     windows_build_tail = f'build\\shared-{tesseract}{build_type}'
801:     
802:     if overwrite_config:
803:         if mupdf_version_tuple >= (1, 28):
804:             # Tell mupdf build to use, for example, `/Build "ReleaseTofuCjkExt|x64"`.
805:             # This avoids the need for us to modify mupdf's config.h.
806:             windows_build_tail += '-TOFU_CJK_EXT'
807:             log(f'Appending, {windows_build_tail=}')
808:         else:
809:             log(f'modifying mupdf:include/mupdf/fitz/config.h')
810:             mupdf_config_h = f'{mupdf_local}/include/mupdf/fitz/config.h'
811:             prefix = '#define TOFU_CJK_EXT 1 /* PyMuPDF override. */\n'
812:             with open(mupdf_config_h) as f:
813:                 text = f.read()
814:             if text.startswith(prefix):
815:                 log(f'Not modifying {mupdf_config_h} because already has prefix {prefix!r}.')
816:             else:
817:                 log(f'Prefixing {mupdf_config_h} with {prefix!r}.')
818:                 text = prefix + text
819:                 st = os.stat(mupdf_config_h)
820:                 with open(mupdf_config_h, 'w') as f:
821:                     f.write(text)
822:                 os.utime(mupdf_config_h, (st.st_atime, st.st_mtime))
823:     
824:     if g_py_limited_api:
825:         windows_build_tail += f'-Py_LIMITED_API_{pipcl.current_py_limited_api()}'
826:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL == '1':
827:         windows_build_tail += '-nogil'
828:     windows_build_tail += f'-{wp.cpu.windows_name}-py{wp.version}'
829:     pipcl.log(f'{sysconfig.get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED")=}')
830:     if sysconfig.get_config_var('Py_GIL_DISABLED')==1:
831:         # We are building with free-threading python.
832:         windows_build_tail += '-t'
833:     windows_build_dir = f'{mupdf_local}\\{windows_build_tail}'
834:     #log( f'Building mupdf.')
835:     devenv = os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_DEVENV')
836:     if not devenv:
837:         try:
838:             # Prefer VS-2022 as that is what Github provide in windows-2022.
839:             log(f'Looking for Visual Studio 2022.')
840:             vs = pipcl.wdev.WindowsVS(year=2022)
841:         except Exception as e:
842:             log(f'Failed to find VS-2022:\n'
843:                     f'{textwrap.indent(traceback.format_exc(), "    ")}'
844:                     )
845:             log(f'Looking for any Visual Studio.')
846:             vs = pipcl.wdev.WindowsVS()
847:         log(f'vs:\n{vs.description_ml("    ")}')
848:         devenv = vs.devenv
849:     if not devenv:
850:         devenv = 'devenv.com'
851:         log( f'Cannot find devenv.com in default locations, using: {devenv!r}')
852:     command = f'cd "{mupdf_local}" && "{sys.executable}" ./scripts/mupdfwrap.py'
853:     if os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_VS_UPGRADE') == '1':
854:         command += ' --vs-upgrade 1'
855:         
856:     # Would like to simply do f'... --devenv {shutil.quote(devenv)}', but
857:     # it looks like if `devenv` has spaces then `shutil.quote()` puts it
858:     # inside single quotes, which then appear to be ignored when run by
859:     # subprocess.run().
860:     #
861:     # So instead we strip any enclosing quotes and the enclose with
862:     # double-quotes.
863:     #
864:     if len(devenv) >= 2:
865:         for q in '"', "'":
866:             if devenv.startswith( q) and devenv.endswith( q):
867:                 devenv = devenv[1:-1]
868:     command += f' -d {windows_build_tail}'
869:     command += f' -b'
870:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF:
871:         command += f' --refcheck-if "{PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF}"'
872:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF:
873:         command += f' --trace-if "{PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF}"'
874:     command += f' --devenv "{devenv}"'
875:     command += f' all'
876:     if os.environ.get( 'PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REBUILD') == '0':
877:         log( f'PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REBUILD is "0" so not building MuPDF; would have run: {command}')
878:     else:
879:         log( f'Building MuPDF by running: {command}')
880:         subprocess.run( command, shell=True, check=True)
881:         log( f'Finished building mupdf.')
882:     
883:     return windows_build_dir
884:

886: def _windows_lib_directory(mupdf_local, build_type):
887:     wc = pipcl.wdev.WindowsCpu()
888:     ret = f'{mupdf_local}/platform/win32/{wc.windows_subdir}'
889:     if build_type == 'release':
890:         ret += 'Release/'
891:     elif build_type == 'debug':
892:         ret += 'Debug/'
893:     else:
894:         assert 0, f'Unrecognised {build_type=}.'
895:     return ret

904: def build_mupdf_unix(
905:         mupdf_local,
906:         build_type,
907:         overwrite_config,
908:         g_py_limited_api,
909:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_REFCHECK_IF,
910:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TRACE_IF,
911:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_SWIG,
912:         PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL,
913:         ):
914:     '''
915:     Builds MuPDF.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         mupdf_local:
919:             Path of MuPDF directory or None if we are using system MuPDF.
920:     
921:     Returns the absolute path of build directory within MuPDF, e.g.
922:     `.../mupdf/build/pymupdf-shared-release`, or `None` if we are using the
923:     system MuPDF.
924:     '''    
925:     if not mupdf_local:
926:         log( f'Using system mupdf.')
927:         return None
928: 
929:     env = dict()
930:     if overwrite_config:
931:         # By predefining TOFU_CJK_EXT here, we don't need to modify
932:         # MuPDF's include/mupdf/fitz/config.h.
933:         log( f'Setting XCFLAGS and XCXXFLAGS to predefine TOFU_CJK_EXT.')
934:         env_add(env, 'XCFLAGS', '-DTOFU_CJK_EXT')
935:         env_add(env, 'XCXXFLAGS', '-DTOFU_CJK_EXT')
936: 
937:     if openbsd or freebsd:
938:         env_add(env, 'CXX', 'c++', ' ')
939:     
940:     if darwin and os.environ.get('GITHUB_ACTIONS') == 'true':
941:         if os.environ.get('ImageOS') == 'macos13':
942:             # On Github macos13 we need to use Clang/LLVM (Homebrew) 15.0.7,
943:             # otherwise mupdf:thirdparty/tesseract/src/api/baseapi.cpp fails to
944:             # compile with:
945:             #
946:             #   thirdparty/tesseract/src/api/baseapi.cpp:150:25: error: 'recursive_directory_iterator' is unavailable: introduced in macOS 10.15
947:             #
948:             # See:
949:             #   https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/macos/macos-13-Readme.md
950:             #
951:             log(f'Using llvm@15 clang and clang++')
952:             cl15 = pipcl.run(f'brew --prefix llvm@15', capture=1)
953:             log(f'{cl15=}')
954:             cl15 = cl15.strip()
955:             pipcl.run(f'ls -lL {cl15}')
956:             pipcl.run(f'ls -lL {cl15}/bin')
957:             cc = f'{cl15}/bin/clang'
958:             cxx = f'{cl15}/bin/clang++'
959:             env['CC'] = cc
960:             env['CXX'] = cxx
961:     
962:     # Show compiler versions.
963:     cc = env.get('CC', 'cc')
964:     cxx = env.get('CXX', 'c++')
965:     pipcl.run(f'{cc} --version')
966:     pipcl.run(f'{cxx} --version')
967: 
968:     # Add extra flags for MacOS cross-compilation, where ARCHFLAGS can be
969:     # '-arch arm64'.
970:     #
971:     archflags = os.environ.get( 'ARCHFLAGS')
972:     if archflags:
973:         env_add(env, 'XCFLAGS', archflags)
974:         env_add(env, 'XLIBS', archflags)
975: 
976:     mupdf_version_tuple = get_mupdf_version(mupdf_local)
977:     
978:     # We specify a build directory path containing 'pymupdf' so that we
979:     # coexist with non-PyMuPDF builds (because PyMuPDF builds have a
980:     # different config.h).
981:     #
982:     # We also append further text to try to allow different builds to
983:     # work if they reuse the mupdf directory.
984:     #
985:     # Using platform.machine() (e.g. 'amd64') ensures that different
986:     # builds of mupdf on a shared filesystem can coexist. Using
987:     # $_PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM allows cross-compiled cibuildwheel builds
988:     # to coexist, e.g. on github.
989:     #
990:     # Have experimented with looking at getconf_ARG_MAX to decide whether to
991:     # omit `PyMuPDF-` from the build directory, to avoid command-too-long
992:     # errors with mupdf-1.26. But it seems that `getconf ARG_MAX` returns
993:     # a system limit, not the actual limit of the current shell, and there
994:     # doesn't seem to be a way to find the current shell's limit.
995:     #
996:     # Avoid link command length problems seen on musllinux.
997:     build_prefix = ''
998:     if pyodide:
999:         build_prefix += 'pyodide-'
1000:     else:
1001:         build_prefix += f'{platform.machine()}-'
1002:     build_prefix_extra = os.environ.get( '_PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM')
1003:     if build_prefix_extra:
1004:         build_prefix += f'{build_prefix_extra}-'
1005:     build_prefix += 'shared-'
1006:     if msys2:
1007:         # Error in mupdf/scripts/tesseract/endianness.h:
1008:         # #error "I don't know what architecture this is!"
1009:         log(f'msys2: building MuPDF without tesseract.')
1010:     elif os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TESSERACT') == '0':
1011:         log(f'PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_TESSERACT=0 so building mupdf without tesseract.')
1012:     else:
1013:         build_prefix += 'tesseract-'
1014:     if (
1015:             linux
1016:             and os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_BSYMBOLIC', '1') == '1'
1017:             ):
1018:         log(f'Appending `bsymbolic-` to MuPDF build path.')
1019:         build_prefix += 'bsymbolic-'
1020:     log(f'{g_py_limited_api=}')
1021:     if g_py_limited_api:
1022:         build_prefix += f'Py_LIMITED_API_{pipcl.current_py_limited_api()}-'
1023:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_FAKE_NOGIL == '1':
1024:         build_prefix += 'nogil-'
1025:     unix_build_dir = f'{mupdf_local}/build/{build_prefix}{build_type}'
1026:     PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_CLEAN = os.environ.get('PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_CLEAN')
1027:     if PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_CLEAN == '1':
1028:         log(f'{PYMUPDF_SETUP_MUPDF_CLEAN=}, deleting {unix_build_dir=}.')
1029:         shutil.rmtree(unix_build_dir, ignore_errors=1)
1030:     # We need MuPDF's Python bindings, so we build MuPDF with
1031:     # `mupdf/scripts/mupdfwrap.py` instead of running `make`.
1032:     #
1033:     command = f'cd {mupdf_local} &&'
1034:     for n, v in env.items():
1035:         command += f' {n}={shlex.quote(v)}'

21: def recoverpix(doc, item):
22:     """Return image for a given XREF."""
23:     x = item[0]  # xref of PDF image
24:     s = item[1]  # xref of its /SMask
25:     if s == 0:  # no smask: use direct image output
26:         return doc.extract_image(x)
27: 
28:     def getimage(pix):
29:         if pix.colorspace.n != 4:
30:             return pix
31:         tpix = pymupdf.Pixmap(pymupdf.csRGB, pix)
32:         return tpix
33: 
34:     # we need to reconstruct the alpha channel with the smask
35:     pix1 = pymupdf.Pixmap(doc, x)
36:     pix2 = pymupdf.Pixmap(doc, s)  # create pixmap of the /SMask entry
37: 
38:     """Sanity check:
39:     - both pixmaps must have the same rectangle
40:     - both pixmaps must have alpha=0
41:     - pix2 must consist of 1 byte per pixel
42:     """
43:     if not (pix1.irect == pix2.irect and pix1.alpha == pix2.alpha == 0 and pix2.n == 1):
44:         pymupdf.message(f"Warning: unsupported /SMask {s} for {x}:")
45:         pymupdf.message(pix2)
46:         pix2 = None
47:         return getimage(pix1)  # return the pixmap as is
48: 
49:     pix = pymupdf.Pixmap(pix1)  # copy of pix1, with an alpha channel added
50:     pix.set_alpha(pix2.samples)  # treat pix2.samples as the alpha values
51:     pix1 = pix2 = None  # free temp pixmaps
52: 
53:     # we may need to adjust something for CMYK pixmaps here:
54:     return getimage(pix)

57: def open_file(filename, password, show=False, pdf=True):
58:     """Open and authenticate a document."""
59:     doc = pymupdf.open(filename)
60:     if not doc.is_pdf and pdf is True:
61:         sys.exit("this command supports PDF files only")
62:     rc = -1
63:     if not doc.needs_pass:
64:         return doc
65:     if password:
66:         rc = doc.authenticate(password)
67:         if not rc:
68:             sys.exit("authentication unsuccessful")
69:         if show is True:
70:             auth_level = "user"
71:             if rc > 2:
72:                 auth_level = "owner"
73:             pymupdf.message(f"authenticated as {auth_level}")
74:     else:
75:         sys.exit(f"'{doc.name}' requires a password")
76:     return doc

110: def get_list(rlist, limit, what="page"):
111:     """Transform a page / xref specification into a list of integers.
112: 
113:     Args
114:     ----
115:         rlist: (str) the specification
116:         limit: maximum number, i.e. number of pages, number of objects
117:         what: a string to be used in error messages
118:     Returns
119:     -------
120:         A list of integers representing the specification.
121:     """
122:     N = str(limit - 1)
123:     rlist = rlist.replace("N", N).replace(" ", "")
124:     rlist_arr = rlist.split(",")
125:     out_list = []
126:     for seq, item in enumerate(rlist_arr):
127:         n = seq + 1
128:         if item.isdecimal():  # a single integer
129:             i = int(item)
130:             if 1 <= i < limit:
131:                 out_list.append(int(item))
132:             else:
133:                 sys.exit(f"bad {what} specification at item {n:d}")
134:             continue
135:         try:  # this must be a range now, and all of the following must work:
136:             i1, i2 = item.split("-")  # will fail if not 2 items produced
137:             i1 = int(i1)  # will fail on non-integers
138:             i2 = int(i2)
139:         except Exception:
140:             sys.exit(f"bad {what} range specification at item {n:d}")
141: 
142:         if not (1 <= i1 < limit and 1 <= i2 < limit):
143:             sys.exit(f"bad {what} range specification at item {n:d}")
144: 
145:         if i1 == i2:  # just in case: a range of equal numbers
146:             out_list.append(i1)
147:             continue
148: 
149:         if i1 < i2:  # first less than second
150:             out_list += list(range(i1, i2 + 1))
151:         else:  # first larger than second
152:             out_list += list(range(i1, i2 - 1, -1))
153: 
154:     return out_list

267: def doc_join(args):
268:     """Join pages from several PDF documents."""
269:     doc_list = args.input  # a list of input PDFs
270:     doc = pymupdf.open()  # output PDF
271:     for src_item in doc_list:  # process one input PDF
272:         src_list = src_item.split(",")
273:         password = src_list[1] if len(src_list) > 1 else None
274:         src = open_file(src_list[0], password, pdf=True)
275:         pages = ",".join(src_list[2:])  # get 'pages' specifications
276:         if pages:  # if anything there, retrieve a list of desired pages
277:             page_list = get_list(",".join(src_list[2:]), src.page_count + 1)
278:         else:  # take all pages
279:             page_list = range(1, src.page_count + 1)
280:         for i in page_list:
281:             doc.insert_pdf(src, from_page=i - 1, to_page=i - 1)  # copy each source page
282:         src.close()
283: 
284:     doc.save(args.output, garbage=4, deflate=True)
285:     doc.close()

556:     eop = b"\n" if noformfeed else bytes([12])
557:     text = page.get_text("text", flags=flags)
558:     if not text:
559:         if not skip_empty:
560:             textout.write(eop)  # write formfeed
561:         return
562:     textout.write(text.encode("utf8", errors="surrogatepass"))
563:     textout.write(eop)
564:     return

568:     eop = b"\n" if noformfeed else bytes([12])
569:     blocks = page.get_text("blocks", flags=flags)
570:     if blocks == []:

584:     # --------------------------------------------------------------------
585:     def find_line_index(values: List[int], value: int) -> int:
586:         """Find the right row coordinate.
587: 
588:         Args:
589:             values: (list) y-coordinates of rows.
590:             value: (int) lookup for this value (y-origin of char).
591:         Returns:
592:             y-ccordinate of appropriate line for value.
593:         """
594:         i = bisect.bisect_right(values, value)
595:         if i:
596:             return values[i - 1]
597:         raise RuntimeError(f"Line for {value:g} not found in {values}")
598: 
599:     # --------------------------------------------------------------------
600:     def curate_rows(rows: Set[int], GRID) -> List:
601:         rows = list(rows)
602:         rows.sort()  # sort ascending
603:         nrows = [rows[0]]
604:         for h in rows[1:]:
605:             if h >= nrows[-1] + GRID:  # only keep significant differences
606:                 nrows.append(h)
607:         return nrows  # curated list of line bottom coordinates
608: 
609:     def process_blocks(blocks: List[Dict], page: pymupdf.Page):
610:         rows = set()
611:         page_width = page.rect.width
612:         page_height = page.rect.height
613:         rowheight = page_height
614:         left = page_width
615:         right = 0

687:     def make_textline(left, slot, minslot, lchars):
688:         """Produce the text of one output line.
689: 
690:         Args:
691:             left: (float) left most coordinate used on page
692:             slot: (float) avg width of one character in any font in use.
693:             minslot: (float) min width for the characters in this line.
694:             chars: (list[tuple]) characters of this line.
695:         Returns:
696:             text: (str) text string for this line
697:         """
698:         text = ""  # we output this
699:         old_char = ""
700:         old_x1 = 0  # end coordinate of last char
701:         old_ox = 0  # x-origin of last char
702:         if minslot <= pymupdf.EPSILON:
703:             raise RuntimeError(f"program error: minslot too small = {minslot:g}")

705:         for c in lchars:  # loop over characters
706:             char, ox, _, cwidth = c
707:             ox = ox - left  # its (relative) start coordinate
708:             x1 = ox + cwidth  # ending coordinate
709: 
710:             # eliminate overprint effect
711:             if old_char == char and ox - old_ox <= cwidth * 0.2:
712:                 continue
713: 
714:             # omit spaces overlapping previous char
715:             if char == " " and (old_x1 - ox) / cwidth > 0.8:
716:                 continue
717: 
718:             old_char = char
719:             # close enough to previous?
720:             if ox < old_x1 + minslot:  # assume char adjacent to previous
721:                 text += char  # append to output
722:                 old_x1 = x1  # new end coord
723:                 old_ox = ox  # new origin.x
724:                 continue
725: 
726:             # else next char starts after some gap:
727:             # fill in right number of spaces, so char is positioned
728:             # in the right slot of the line
729:             if char == " ":  # rest relevant for non-space only
730:                 continue
731:             delta = int(ox / slot) - len(text)
732:             if ox > old_x1 and delta > 1:
733:                 text += " " * delta
734:             # now append char
735:             text += char
736:             old_x1 = x1  # new end coordinate
737:             old_ox = ox  # new origin

773:     # The minimum char width of each line is used to determine if spaces must

800:         textout.write((text + "\n").encode("utf8", errors="surrogatepass"))

55:     """Return the text blocks on a page.
56: 
57:     Notes:
58:         Lines in a block are concatenated with line breaks.
59:     Args:
60:         flags: (int) control the amount of data parsed into the textpage.
61:     Returns:
62:         A list of the blocks. Each item contains the containing rectangle
63:         coordinates, text lines, running block number and block type.
64:     """
65:     pymupdf.CheckParent(page)
66:     if flags is None:
67:         flags = pymupdf.TEXTFLAGS_BLOCKS
68:     tp = textpage

70:         tp = page.get_textpage(clip=clip, flags=flags)
71:     elif getattr(tp, "parent") != page:
72:         raise ValueError("not a textpage of this page")
73: 
74:     blocks = tp.extractBLOCKS()
75:     if textpage is None:

82: def get_text_words(

92: 
93:     Args:
94:         page: pymupdf.Page
95:         clip: (rect-like) area on page to consider
96:         flags: (int) control the amount of data parsed into the textpage.
97:         textpage: (pymupdf.TextPage) either passed-in or None.
98:         sort: (bool) sort the words in reading sequence.
99:         delimiters: (str,list) characters to use as word delimiters.
100:         tolerance: (float) consider words to be part of the same line if
101:             top or bottom coordinate are not larger than this. Relevant
102:             only if sort=True.
103: 
104:     Returns:
105:         Word tuples (x0, y0, x1, y1, "word", bno, lno, wno).
106:     """

108:     def sort_words(words):
109:         """Sort words line-wise, forgiving small deviations."""
110:         words.sort(key=lambda w: (w[3], w[0]))
111:         nwords = []  # final word list
112:         line = [words[0]]  # collects words roughly in same line
113:         lrect = pymupdf.Rect(words[0][:4])  # start the line rectangle
114:         for w in words[1:]:
115:             wrect = pymupdf.Rect(w[:4])
116:             if (
117:                 abs(wrect.y0 - lrect.y0) <= tolerance
118:                 or abs(wrect.y1 - lrect.y1) <= tolerance
119:             ):
120:                 line.append(w)
121:                 lrect |= wrect
122:             else:
123:                 line.sort(key=lambda w: w[0])  # sort words in line l-t-r
124:                 nwords.extend(line)  # append to final words list
125:                 line = [w]  # start next line
126:                 lrect = wrect  # start next line rect
127: 
128:         line.sort(key=lambda w: w[0])  # sort words in line l-t-r
129:         nwords.extend(line)  # append to final words list
130: 
131:         return nwords
132: 
133:     pymupdf.CheckParent(page)
134:     if flags is None:
135:         flags = pymupdf.TEXTFLAGS_WORDS
136:     tp = textpage
137:     if tp is None:
138:         tp = page.get_textpage(clip=clip, flags=flags)
139:     elif getattr(tp, "parent") != page:
140:         raise ValueError("not a textpage of this page")

142:     words = tp.extractWORDS(delimiters)

150:         ]

152:     if textpage is None:
153:         del tp
154:     if words and sort:
155:         # advanced sort if any words found
156:         words = sort_words(words)
157: 
158:     return words

175:                 pymupdf.log(f'{os.getpid()=}: sending {page_num=} {ret=}')

314:     page: pymupdf.Page,
315:     flags: int = 0,
316:     language: str = "eng",
317:     dpi: int = 72,
318:     full: bool = False,
319:     tessdata: str = None,
320: ) -> pymupdf.TextPage:
321:     """Create a Textpage from the OCR version of the page.
322: 
323:     OCR can be executed for the full page image, or (the default) only
324:     for areas that are not covered by readable digital text.
325: 
326:     Args:
327:         flags: (int) control content becoming part of the result.
328:         language: (str) specify expected language(s). Default is "eng" (English).
329:         dpi: (int) resolution in dpi, default 72.
330:         full: (bool) whether to OCR the full page, or to keep legible text
331:         tessdata: (str) path to Tesseract language data files. If None, the
332:                   built-in function is used to find the path.
333:     """
334:     pymupdf.CheckParent(page)
335:     tessdata = pymupdf.get_tessdata(tessdata)
336: 
337:     # Ensure 0xFFFD is not suppressed
338:     flags = (
339:         flags
340:         & ~pymupdf.TEXT_USE_CID_FOR_UNKNOWN_UNICODE  # pylint: disable=no-member
341:         & ~pymupdf.TEXT_USE_GID_FOR_UNKNOWN_UNICODE  # pylint: disable=no-member
342:     )
343: 
344:     def full_ocr(page, dpi, language, flags):
345:         """Perform OCR for the full page image."""
346:         pix = page.get_pixmap(dpi=dpi)
347:         # create a 1-page PDF with an OCR text layer.
348:         ocr_pdf = pymupdf.Document(
349:             stream=pix.pdfocr_tobytes(
350:                 compress=False,
351:                 language=language,
352:                 tessdata=tessdata,
353:             ),
354:         )
355:         ocr_page = ocr_pdf.load_page(0)
356:         unzoom = page.rect.width / ocr_page.rect.width
357:         ctm = pymupdf.Matrix(unzoom, unzoom) * page.derotation_matrix
358:         tpage = ocr_page.get_textpage(flags=flags, matrix=ctm)
359: 
360:         # associate the textpage with the original page
361:         tpage.parent = weakref.proxy(page)
362:         return tpage
363: 
364:     def partial_ocr(page, dpi, language, flags):
365:         """Perform OCR for parts of the page without legible text.
366: 
367:         We create a temporary PDF for which we can freely redact text.
368:         """
369:         doc = page.parent
370: 
371:         # make temporary PDF with the passed-in page
372:         temp_pdf = pymupdf.open()
373:         temp_pdf.insert_pdf(doc, from_page=page.number, to_page=page.number)
374:         temp_page = temp_pdf.load_page(0)
375:         temp_page.remove_rotation()  # avoid OCR problems with rotated pages
376: 
377:         # extract text bboxes from the page
378:         tp = temp_page.get_textpage(flags=flags)
379:         blocks = tp.extractDICT()["blocks"]
380: 
381:         """
382:         For partial OCR we need a TextPage that contains legible text only.
383:         Illegible text must be passed to the OCR engine.
384:         """
385:         # Select spans with illegible text. If present, remove them first.
386:         fffd_spans = [
387:             s["bbox"]
388:             for b in blocks
389:             if b["type"] == 0
390:             for l in b["lines"]
391:             for s in l["spans"]
392:             if chr(0xFFFD) in s["text"]
